title: Modular persistent storage Terraform: upgrade safety and runtime health checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reusable Terraform module that standardizes EBS/EFS/S3 constructs, snapshot lifecycle, and KMS-first encryption defaults for Private (VPC) deployments, and define a safe major-version upgrade path plus runtime health checks. The module must be opinionated but configurable: enforce encryption-at-rest, strong IAM boundaries, sane lifecycle policies, and offer a zero-downtime upgrade playbook for storage schema/provider changes.

Motivation: Several private deployments have ad-hoc storage IaC with drift and inconsistent snapshot policies. We need a single source-of-truth module to reduce incidents and accelerate upgrades for on-prem/VPC customers.

Scope: Terraform module + test harness + rollout playbook + health-check lambdas. Not in scope: application migration tooling or data-plane replication between regions (future work).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Module exposes inputs for: ebs_enabled (bool), ebs_type, ebs_encrypted_kms_key_id, efs_enabled, efs_throughput_mode, s3_buckets (map), s3_encryption_kms_key_id, snapshot_retention_days, cross_account_snapshot (bool). 2) Defaults enforce encryption (EBS/EFS/S3) using customer-managed KMS key aliases with rotation enabled. 3) Terraform plan must show no destructive changes for minor version upgrades when using the upgrade helper. 4) Automated health checks detect lost snapshots, unencrypted volumes, or drift and raise alerts in Grafana/Slack. 5) CI integration with terratest/step functions validates create/update/destroy against a small sandbox VPC. 6) Playbook tested in staging with a canary tenant and documented rollback steps.
tasks:
1) Design module interface and default policy (Aisha)
2) Implement core resources: aws_ebs_volume/aws_ebs_snapshot, aws_efs_file_system/aws_efs_mount_target, aws_s3_bucket (Miguel)
3) KMS key creation/alias + rotation module (security)
4) Snapshot lifecycle lambda + verifier job (DevOps)
5) Terraform upgrade helper script (safe-apply pattern)
6) Terratest suite and CI job (integration)
7) Run staged upgrade against canary tenant and capture metrics (observability)
8) Documentation + Confluence runbook + console dashboard tiles
9) Security review and compliance sign-off

Status per task: 1: done, 2: in progress, 3: blocked (KMS policy review), 4: in progress, 5: in progress, 6: planned, 7: planned, 8: planned, 9: planned
decisions:
- Encryption defaults: enforce SSE-KMS for S3, EBS encryption enabled=true, EFS encrypted=true. Customers can supply their KMS key id; module will create a key only when kms_create=true.
- Snapshot retention: default 30d for EBS snapshots, 90d for EFS backups, configurable.
- Cross-account snapshots off by default; enable will create least-privileged IAM role and snapshot sharing policy.
- Terraform state: recommend remote backend in our S3 bucket with state-locking via DynamoDB; the module will emit recommended backend config, but not manage it directly.
- Upgrade model: adopt a 3-step safe-apply helper: plan -> preflight verifier (snapshot+locks) -> staged apply with canary instance -> full rollout.
- Health checks: implement lightweight Lambda that runs daily verifying: snapshot consistency, KMS key policy integrity, bucket encryption, and mount target reachability. Alerts go to #infra-private and to a Grafana alert rule.

notes_for_release: When cutting private-2026.1 include upgrade-helper script, health-check lambda, and the terratest pipeline. Coordinate release with support so we can schedule maintenance windows for existing private tenants that opt into the module upgrade.
rollback_plan: 1) If a staged apply causes regression, execute terraform apply against canary with previous module version saved as module_source = git://...@v0.9.2. 2) Restore EBS from prior snapshot (automated snapshot restore playbook). 3) Recreate IAM policies from snapshot of previous state. 4) Open a P0 incident and route to oncall-storage. 5) Postmortem within 72 hours.
qa_plan:
- Terratest: create -> attach -> snapshot -> verify snapshot metadata -> destroy.
- Security tests: verify KMS key rotation policy and key policy simulation.
- Chaos test: simulate API throttling and S3 eventual consistency in a sandbox and verify verifier lambda handles transient failures.
- Upgrade test: run major-version bump in staging with the helper; confirm no data loss and terraform plan shows non-destructive changes.
operational_playbook: Pre-upgrade checklist: ensure latest snapshots for all volumes (age < 2h), verify KMS key policy contains redwood-infra role, disable automatic destructive changes in pipeline, set maintenance window, notify customers, create stakeholder channel. Post-upgrade: run full health-check, validate Grafana metrics, escalate if errors > 1% of volumes.
